study: Range entry on the desk: buy low in the support->resistance gap with %R trending up (operator's model), exit at resistance - does it make money in the nightly replay on the desk's own names, feed and costs, and beat the live entry?
registered_at: 2026-10-08 ~18:30 ET, before the variant exists in code and before any replay of it
origin: Operator 10/8 (SPCX charts): 'a gap between support and resistance and trending up with %R' is how the indicators are expected to behave. The live desk arms at/near overbought, which on such charts is just under resistance (10/5-10/8 fills 0-0.1% under resistance: n 20, -10 bp, 20% win).
prior: LOW. sr_range_trade (10/5, SIP, flat 0.20% cost, 485 trades) FAILED: net -15 bp, gross +4.9 bp, and -4.7 bp vs a same-bracket random up-minute. Differences here: the desk's live code, IEX bars, real per-name spreads (tight names ~1-3 bp), the engine %R line, the desk's names. A pass must therefore clear a fresh bar on new sessions; the 10/5 data are not reused.

arms.range_arm: scripts/tight_trail_replay.sh: R range_arm --set ai_watch_range_arm=true --set ai_exit_range=true (entries ONLY from the range rule; square/presquare arms off; exits per 'exit' below)
arms.reference: the replay's base run of the same session (the live config of that day, presquare-only from 10/09)

entry: at a book check (all other live admission/arm gates unchanged: sources, price, spread, 10:30 start, levered deny): (a) a charted support block is at or below the price and the price is 0.00-0.30% above that block's top, or inside it (ob_sup_pct in [0, 0.30]); (b) a charted resistance block is above with ob_room_pct >= 0.40 (price not inside resistance); (c) the ENGINE fast %R (dashboard signal_proximity, minute-grid line; never the live clock-window recompute) is < -20 and higher than on the previous DISTINCT engine read; engine read age <= 90 s. Order-block readings older than 240 s (store age) = no reading = no arm. Levels at the arm are recorded on the position: support bottom S_btm, resistance bottom R_btm. (a), (b), S_btm and R_btm all come from ONE ob_observe._charted_at(sym, now) call at the check price, never from the indicator dict (which carries the previous poll's stamp); max(block.known_ts) is logged per arm and must be <= floor(now, 60). Order-block staleness: no reading when the newest closed bar in the ob store is > 240 s older than now (bar time, as run_manager); _ob_reading_stale also applies; both counts logged.
exit: first of: TARGET price >= R_btm x (1 - 0.0002) (sell at the triggering poll's price); STOP price < S_btm - $0.01; TIME 30 min after entry; 15:50 flatten. The ratchet, decay leash, no-progress cut, dead-trade, triangle and %R dump are OFF for range_arm positions. Size and the order path unchanged.
sessions: the first 12 sessions on which the build passes the per-input check, from 2026-10-09 or the first session after the build ships; ONE read at session 12; nightly numbers are direction only.
per_input_check: the replay fills the ob store SYNCHRONOUSLY from its day_bars IEX cache (completed minutes only; no background warm thread). Per session: share of range_arm book checks with an order-block reading (support and resistance side), share with a fresh engine read, counts of checks failing (a), (b), (c) alone, count of range arms. Replaying session 1 twice must give identical range_arm trades, else BUILD FAILURE. A session is a BUILD FAILURE if order-block readings exist on < 70% of checks or engine reads are fresh on < 50%. More than 3 build failures, or trades on fewer than 8 of the 12 counted sessions -> VACUOUS (not read). Development runs report only per-input counts, never range_arm or control P&L; sessions replayed before the build ships are never counted.
statistic: per trade net bp = exit/entry - 1 at the replay fill MINUS the full SIP quoted spread at entry (tools/studies/replay_costing.py), applied identically to range_arm, the reference and the control; a trade with no NBBO is charged that arm's median spread for the day (never dropped; count reported per session). Per-day mean; mean over days with t across days (df = days - 1). Entries AND exits are re-scored at the next poll and at +10 s; the pass must hold under all three entry x exit fill rules. Reference pairing: days on which either arm has 0 trades are left out of the paired difference (counted).
pass: at the single read: range_arm net per trade > 0 with t >= 2 across days under all three fill rules, >= 60 trades, negative on <= 30% of days, still > 0 after dropping the best day and (separately) the top 5 symbols by P&L; AND range_arm minus control >= +3 bp with t >= 2 across days (the location test the 10/5 study failed); AND range_arm minus the reference >= +3 bp with t >= 2 (paired by day). A pass earns a skeptic review of the positive, then a live paper switch-on; not live money (live_mirror_week_prereg.json amended_4).
fail: range_arm net per trade <= 0 at >= 60 trades, or paired difference <= -3 bp with t <= -2 -> FAIL; otherwise CLOSED UNPROVEN. Either closes the range-entry question for the current level source (LuxAlgo order-block port).
information_only: range_arm exit reason mix (target / stop / time / flatten) and net per reason
win rate, median room to resistance at entry, median ob_sup_pct at entry
tight vs movers split kept visible (the ~0.38% minimum target leaves room on tight spreads, not on movers)
no_retuning: the 0.30% support band, 0.40% room, %R < -20 rising, the exits and the 12-session read are fixed; any change is a new pre-registration
caveats: replay recall of live buys was ~27% on 10/7: the comparison is variant vs reference inside the replay
order-block levels are the LuxAlgo port (TradingView mismatch on thin premarket names, 10/7 chart check)
the target assumes a fill at the triggering poll's price (no queue model)
control: for each range_arm trade, one random minute (fixed seed 71, sha256 of symbol|day|entry minute) in the same name, day and ET clock hour where the engine fast %R is below -20 and rising, NOT within 10 min of the trade, with the same % target and % stop distances and the same 30-min time stop, entered at that minute's IEX 1-min close, exits scanned on later IEX 1-min bars (stop wins a same-bar tie), the same spread charged. No legal minute in that hour -> the next later hour, then the earlier (counted).
amended: 2026-10-08 ~19:00 ET, before any code or replay: skeptic FIX FIRST (8) applied - spread charged via replay_costing (no-NBBO = day median, never dropped); bar-time 240 s ob staleness plus _ob_reading_stale; levels from one _charted_at call at the check price with known_ts logged; synchronous ob store in the replay, determinism re-run, 70% coverage; same-bracket random-minute location control; entry and exit fill re-scoring; best-day and top-5-symbol drops; development runs blind to P&L. Notes: reference pairing on zero-trade days, tight/movers split.
